canon.note: Exiled priest and prophet at the river Chebar.

stages.text: Ezekiel son of Buzi: a man of about thirty, lean and steady, with dark hair and a short trimmed beard, bronze-brown skin from desert sun, and a calm, watchful face. He wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic with a long cloak of rough brown wool over it. He carries a wooden writing tablet and stylus.

canon.name: Man clothed in linen
canon.note: Heavenly figure who marks the faithful with a mark, scatters coals over the city, and measures the new temple with a reed; treated as one guide throughout Ezekiel.

stages.label: Man clothed in linen

quotes.quote: the man clothed in linen, who had the writer’s inkhorn by his side
Take fire from between the whirling wheels, from between the cherubim

stages.text: Man clothed in linen: a figure of mature, steady presence, neither young nor old; lean and upright build; pale bronze skin with a faint radiance; close-cut dark hair and short beard; calm, grave features. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic and priestly linen sash, plain and unadorned. Carries a scribe's bronze inkhorn at his side and a measuring reed of cane in hand.

canon.name: Ezekiel's temple
canon.note: The Jerusalem temple of Ezekiel's visions of abominations and the measured new temple.

stages.label: Ezekiel's temple

quotes.quote: so that there was the face of a man toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other side.
There were made on them, on the doors of the nave, cherubim and palm trees, like those made on the walls.
He measured the court, one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide, square. The altar was before the house.

stages.text: Ezekiel's temple: a walled sanctuary on the mountain of Jerusalem, built of pale dressed limestone with cedar panelling, its inner court paved and square, its nave carved with cherubim and palm trees between which a face of a man and a face of a young lion alternate. Gates of the outer court face east, north and south; side chambers rise in three stories. Olive and cedar trees line the courts; a river flows from beneath the threshold.

fields.primarySubject: The man clothed in linen stands at the southern gate's post, measuring rod in hand; Ezekiel stands a step behind him, watching.
fields.action: The man clothed in linen measures the gatepost's height with a rod while Ezekiel observes; Ezekiel's hands rest quietly at his sides.
fields.setting: A stone gate of the outer temple precinct in the inner court, massive dressed stone posts and a rounded arch, with a stone pavement and bronze-cornered measuring tools on the ground.
fields.secondaryElements: A measuring reed and cord lie on the pavement; a bronze measuring rod in the man's hand; the arches and posts are shown in careful proportion.
fields.mood: Reverent and quiet, with a sense of ordered holiness and patient attention.
fields.timeOfDay: Clear daylight falling evenly across the stone.
fields.composition: Eye-level view from within the court, the gate centered and receding slightly, with the measuring figure and Ezekiel in the foreground and the arch framing the upper space.

look.place: Interior courtyard threshold of a visionary temple complex, with a stone gate facing south, pale limestone walls and a measuring cord laid on the ground.
look.timeOfDay: Early morning light, the same clear hour throughout the section.
look.weather: Still, clear air with a faint haze of cloud high above.
look.light: Soft dawn light from the south, with a veiled radiance of white-gold and a fire-like glow resting at the edges of the gate.
look.clothing: Priestly linen tunics and a linen cord and measuring reed carried by the guide; plain sandals and dust on the stone.

canon.name: Absalom
canon.note: Son of David who revolts and is killed by Joab.

stages.label: Absalom, son of David

quotes.quote: From the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no defect in him.
Absalom prepared a chariot and horses for himself, and fifty men to run before him.
Absalom was riding on his mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak

stages.text: Absalom: a young man of about twenty, lean and upright, with an unblemished, strikingly handsome face; olive-brown skin; thick dark hair worn long to the shoulders; a short, full beard trimmed close; dark, clear eyes. Signature outfit: a fine undyed linen tunic with a deep blue court cloak edged in gold thread. Signature prop: a mule, which he rides, and nothing else he carries alone.

aliases: the anointed of the God of Jacob
canon.name: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)
canon.note: The single David of the Hebrew books and the New Testament references: son of Jesse, shepherd, harpist, anointed king, father of Solomon; all entries describe this one king and the hint's second David is not needed.

stages.label: David as king

quotes.quote: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

stages.text: David: a man of about thirty to fifty, athletic and broad-shouldered, of medium height; ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes, short dark beard trimmed close; dark hair cut to the shoulder. Signature outfit: a long blue royal robe with a sash of crimson and gold, over an undertunic of white linen. Carries a bronze-bossed sword in a leather scabbard and a harp.

stages.label: David as youth

quotes.quote: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”

stages.text: David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.

stages.label: David as elder

quotes.quote: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.

stages.text: David: an old man of about seventy, lean and bent with age, his frame still dignified; ruddy complexion faded to a weathered warmth, dark eyes deep-set and gentle, white hair and a white beard cut short. Signature outfit: a plain long wool robe of undyed cream with a dark blue cloak over the shoulders for warmth. Carries a staff of almond wood.

canon.name: Jonadab son of Shimeah
canon.note: David's nephew, son of Shimeah and Amnon's friend in 2 Samuel who devises the plot against Tamar; distinct from Jonadab son of Rechab.

stages.label: Jonadab son of Shimeah

quotes.quote: Jonadab was a very subtle man.

stages.text: Jonadab son of Shimeah: a man in his late twenties to thirties; lean, medium build; olive skin; short dark beard trimmed close; narrow, watchful face with a thoughtful brow. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of dark blue-grey wool beneath a court robe of deep ochre, with a plain linen headcloth. He carries no props.

canon.name: David's royal palace in Jerusalem
canon.note: The king's house in Jerusalem where David's scenes unfold (Bathsheba, Uriah, Nathan, Amnon and Tamar); distinguish from the other royal houses by its Davidic setting.

stages.label: David's royal palace in Jerusalem

quotes.quote: went up to the room over the gate and wept

stages.text: David's royal palace in Jerusalem: a substantial citadel of dressed ashlar stone and cedar-beamed timber, set on the ridge of the City of David above the Kidron valley. Flat-roofed stone halls rise in terraces, with a gate tower of heavy masonry whose upper chamber, the room over the gate, has latticed windows. Olive trees and terraced vineyards grow on the slopes below; cypress and terebinth stand near the walls.

fields.action: David sits in mourning, head lowered, hands resting heavily in his lap, sorrowing through the quiet days.
fields.setting: An inner chamber of David's royal palace in Jerusalem, with stone walls and a low couch, dim with the stillness of mourning.
fields.secondaryElements: A closed doorway in the background, a scroll lying unopened on a table, a lamp burning low and steady.
fields.mood: Deep sorrow, quiet, enduring grief tempered with dignity.
fields.timeOfDay: Dusk light falling through a high window into the chamber.

fields.primarySubject: A goldsmith with lowered hands before a finished molten image of metal, its surface unmoving.

canon.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord
canon.note: The one Jesus: the teacher from Nazareth of the Gospels and Acts, and the risen, exalted Christ and Lord of the epistles and Revelation; the same individual across all divisions, with death, resurrection and changed portrayal not creating new individuals.

stages.label: Adult Jesus

quotes.quote: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

stages.text: Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

stages.label: Infant Jesus

quotes.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

canon.name: the Pharisees
canon.note: The Pharisees as a religious party opposing Jesus over Sabbath, purity, tradition and table fellowship; all four Gospel entries describe this same party, so they form one cluster.

stages.label: the Pharisees

quotes.quote: The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat.
like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful

stages.text: The Pharisees: a typical member of the party is a man of middle age to elderly, with a lean, serious build; olive skin weathered by travel; a close-cut or short-bearded face with a grave, watchful expression; hair kept neatly under a head covering. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a dark blue-violet cloak and tassel fringes at the corners. Signature prop: a small phylactery box on the forehead and forearm, and a scroll of the law.

canon.name: Galilee
canon.note: The northern region of Galilee where Jesus preaches, teaches and heals; both Matthew and Luke describe the same region, so these entries are one place.

stages.label: Galilee

quotes.quote: Walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers
teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom
toward the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles

stages.text: Galilee: Northern hill country falling to a freshwater lake, the sea of Galilee, its shore lined with fishing boats and nets drying on stone. Low limestone villages of flat-roofed houses, a white stone synagogue with a shallow portico, terraced olive groves, fig trees and scrubland. Roman roads and a distant Gentile town on the slopes.

fields.primarySubject: A servant standing before his master, hands open in report.
fields.action: The servant gives his report to the master, who is reclining or seated at the banquet, while empty places remain at the table.
fields.setting: A wealthy house's banquet hall in Roman Judea, with a long table, couches, and lamplight.
fields.secondaryElements: Oil lamps on stands, a laden table with bread and cups, a few empty couches and cushioned seats left unoccupied.
fields.mood: Expectant and sober, with a quiet sense of unfinished welcome.
fields.timeOfDay: Evening, lit by oil lamps and the last warm light from an open doorway.
fields.composition: Medium shot from the side, servant in the foreground facing the master, the table and empty seats stretching into the background.

look.timeOfDay: Evening, the banquet hour
look.weather: Clear and warm, dry air with a faint breeze

look.clothing: Tunics, cloaks and head coverings typical of Galilean Jews, with a servant's simple work clothes and some cloaks worn against the evening chill

moment.text: to confirm these days of Purim in their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had decreed, and as they had imposed upon themselves and their descendants in the matter of the fastings and their mourning.

previous.text: He sent letters to all the Jews in the hundred twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus with words of peace and truth,

next.text: The commandment of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.

canon.name: Mordecai
canon.note: Benjamite Jew in Susa who refuses to bow to Haman.

stages.label: Mordecai

quotes.quote: There was a certain Jew in the citadel of Susa whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair
Mordecai tore his clothes and put on sackcloth with ashes
Mordecai went out of the presence of the king in royal clothing of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold

stages.text: Mordecai: a Benjamite Jew of middle years, lean and upright, with dark brown skin, close-cut graying hair and a short trimmed beard. Lined, steady face with deep-set dark eyes. Usual dress: a plain undyed linen tunic and a dark brown woollen cloak. Carries a plain wooden staff of office at the gate.

canon.name: Esther
canon.note: Jewish orphan niece of Mordecai, made queen to replace Vashti, who hides her identity and intercedes for her people in Persia; not the same as the Sheba queen or the unnamed queen of Daniel.

stages.label: Esther

quotes.quote: The maiden was fair and beautiful
he set the royal crown on her head
the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand
Esther put on her royal clothing

stages.text: Esther: a young woman of about twenty, slender and graceful in build, with warm olive-brown skin and dark hair braided and bound up beneath a fine veil. Her face is gentle and dignified, with large dark eyes and a calm, grave bearing. Her signature outfit is a long court robe of deep crimson silk with a gold-embroidered border, a gold belt, and gold bangles at the wrists. When received before the king she wears the royal crown of gold. She alone carries the king's golden scepter.

canon.name: The Jews in Esther
canon.note: Jews across the provinces of Persia who defend themselves, defeat enemies and establish Purim.

stages.label: The Jews in Esther

quotes.quote: many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
the Jews gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces

stages.text: The Jews in Esther: a people of all ages, from children to elders; typical adults of middle stature with sturdy, unhurried builds; olive to tawny skin; dark hair worn to the shoulder or bound, men with short, full beards; plain undyed linen and wool tunics with long cloaks in earth tones of brown, ochre and undyed cream; sackcloth and ashes in mourning.

aliases: the kingdom from India to Ethiopia
canon.name: the provinces
canon.note: The 127 provinces of the empire where decrees are sent and the Jews live.

stages.label: the provinces

quotes.quote: the governors and princes of the provinces which are from India to Ethiopia, one hundred twenty-seven provinces
the army of Persia and Media, the nobles and princes of the provinces

stages.text: the provinces: a vast realm of 127 provinces spanning from India to Ethiopia; wide river plains, dry steppe and desert, date palms and tamarisk along irrigation canals, walled cities of sun-dried brick and stone with gates, royal roads with milestones, Persian palaces with columned halls, and village settlements of mudbrick houses.

fields.primarySubject: Mordecai and Esther standing together, side by side, in a dignified posture of authority and shared resolve.
fields.action: Mordecai and Esther stand before the assembled Jews, confirming the days of Purim as their decree is read aloud from an open scroll held by a scribe.
fields.setting: A stone-columned royal hall in Susa, with sunlight falling through high windows onto polished floors.
fields.secondaryElements: A scribe holds an open scroll unrolled between Mordecai and Esther; a crowd of Jews in plain tunics and cloaks gathers attentively before them.
fields.mood: Solemn, grateful and grounded, with a quiet sense of communal dignity.
fields.timeOfDay: Midday, with clear natural light entering the hall.
fields.composition: Medium-wide frontal view from slightly below the dais, Mordecai and Esther centered, the scribe and scroll at their midline, the assembly filling the lower foreground.

stages.text: Isaiah son of Amoz: a man in his fifties, lean and sinewy, with a weathered brown skin of the Judean hill country. stages.text: Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. stages.text: Joash: a boy of about seven at his crowning, slight and small-boned, with a young, solemn face, olive-brown skin, and short dark curls. He carries a small bronze-handled scroll of the covenant.

canon.name: Zechariah son of Jehoiada (priest)

stages.text: Zechariah son of Jehoiada: a man of middle years, lean and upright, with a dignified, weathered face and dark, close-cropped beard streaked with grey; olive skin and a calm, grave bearing. He wears white priestly linen: a long linen tunic with a sash of blue, violet and scarlet, and a linen cap, all in white and blue. He carries no props alone.

stages.text: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

stages.text: Horeb/Mount Sinai: a single steep granite mountain rising from a stark desert wilderness of rock and sand; its lower slopes are broken boulders and gravel, its upper peak sharp and dark, with a cloud-wrapped summit. The base is marked by a rocky plain where the people camp, bounded by stones. No vegetation beyond scattered desert shrub; the mountain has no buildings.

moment.text: The waters rose, and increased greatly on the earth; and the ship floated on the surface of the waters.

canon.name: Noah
canon.note: The righteous patriarch of Genesis who builds the ark, survives the flood, and has sons Shem, Ham and Japheth; the same Noah is alluded to in Matthew, Hebrews, 1 Peter and 2 Peter as a historical example, so all Noah entries form one cluster.

stages.label: Noah

quotes.quote: Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time. Noah walked with God.
Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters came on the earth.

stages.text: Noah: man of about six hundred years, weathered and sturdy from a lifetime of farming and shipbuilding; broad-shouldered, lean, with deep lines at the eyes and brow; skin sun-browned; long grey hair and a full grey beard, kept untrimmed; calm, steady, dignified face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic in earth brown under a rough wool wrap in ochre, with leather sandals. Carries a carpenter's adze or a simple wooden staff, nothing else.

canon.name: Noah's ark
canon.note: The gopher-wood vessel built at God's command to carry Noah's family and the animals through the flood; not a ship at sea in the Jonah or Acts sense.

stages.label: The ark

quotes.quote: Make a ship of gopher wood. You shall make rooms in the ship

stages.text: Noah's ark: a vast wooden vessel of gopher wood, roughly three hundred cubits long, fifty wide and thirty high, built in three levels with a roof finished a cubit upward. Its planks are sealed inside and out with dark pitch. A single door is set in its side. Its timbers are weathered grey-brown where the flood water has washed over them.

fields.primarySubject: Noah, standing on the deck of the great wooden ark, one hand resting on the rail.

fields.mood: Sombre, grieved and quietly resolute.

canon.name: Joash king of Judah

canon.name: Zechariah son of Jehoiada (priest)

stages.label: Zechariah son of Jehoiada, priest

quotes.quote: The Spirit of God came on Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest

stages.text: Zechariah son of Jehoiada: a man of middle years, lean and upright, with a dignified, weathered face and dark, close-cropped beard streaked with grey; olive skin and a calm, grave bearing. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

fields.primarySubject: Unnamed villagers in mid-flight along a dusty road, one fugitive glancing back over the shoulder.
fields.action: The fugitive turns his head toward the hills behind him while the villagers hurry forward carrying bundled belongings.
fields.setting: Terraced hillside of Judah with a dusty road and worn stone terraces, the land itself present as the setting.
fields.secondaryElements: Bundled belongings on shoulders, worn tunics and travel cloaks, sandals raising dust; no written elements.
fields.mood: Urgent, sorrowful, dignified flight under a heavy sky.
fields.timeOfDay: Late afternoon shifting toward dusk, diffused golden-grey daylight dimming warmly.
fields.composition: Wide view from behind the fleeing group, road leading into the distance, figures small against the terraced hillside.

look.place: Ruined village hillside of Judah with terraced fields, a dusty road and distant city walls; a path leading toward Jerusalem's gate, and an empty seat of stone on a rise
look.timeOfDay: Late afternoon shifting into dusk across the section
look.weather: Dry, still air with low drifting dust and a heavy veil of slow-moving cloud
look.light: Diffused golden-grey daylight dimming warmly; the distant radiant glow of divine presence as a fire-like brilliance behind the cloud
look.clothing: Travel cloaks, worn tunics, sandals and bundled belongings carried by the fleeing villagers

moment.text: to confirm these days of Purim in their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had decreed, and as they had imposed upon themselves and their descendants in the matter of the fastings and their mourning.

previous.text: He sent letters to all the Jews in the hundred twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus with words of peace and truth,

next.text: The commandment of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.

canon.name: Mordecai
canon.note: Benjamite Jew in Susa who refuses to bow to Haman.

stages.label: Mordecai

quotes.quote: There was a certain Jew in the citadel of Susa whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair
Mordecai tore his clothes and put on sackcloth with ashes
Mordecai went out of the presence of the king in royal clothing of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold

stages.text: Mordecai: a Benjamite Jew of middle years, lean and upright, with dark brown skin, close-cut graying hair and a short trimmed beard. Lined, steady face with deep-set dark eyes. Usual dress: a plain undyed linen tunic and a dark brown woollen cloak. Carries a plain wooden staff of office at the gate.

canon.name: Esther
canon.note: Jewish orphan niece of Mordecai, made queen to replace Vashti, who hides her identity and intercedes for her people in Persia; not the same as the Sheba queen or the unnamed queen of Daniel.

stages.label: Esther

quotes.quote: The maiden was fair and beautiful
he set the royal crown on her head
the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand
Esther put on her royal clothing

stages.text: Esther: a young woman of about twenty, slender and graceful in build, with warm olive-brown skin and dark hair braided and bound up beneath a fine veil. Her face is gentle and dignified, with large dark eyes and a calm, grave bearing. Her signature outfit is a long court robe of deep crimson silk with a gold-embroidered border, a gold belt, and gold bangles at the wrists. When received before the king she wears the royal crown of gold. She alone carries the king's golden scepter.

canon.name: The Jews in Esther
canon.note: Jews across the provinces of Persia who defend themselves, defeat enemies and establish Purim.

stages.label: The Jews in Esther

quotes.quote: many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
the Jews gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces

stages.text: The Jews in Esther: a people of all ages, from children to elders; typical adults of middle stature with sturdy, unhurried builds; olive to tawny skin; dark hair worn to the shoulder or bound, men with short, full beards; plain undyed linen and wool tunics with long cloaks in earth tones of brown, ochre and undyed cream; sackcloth and ashes in mourning.

aliases: the kingdom from India to Ethiopia
canon.name: the provinces
canon.note: The 127 provinces of the empire where decrees are sent and the Jews live.

stages.label: the provinces

quotes.quote: the governors and princes of the provinces which are from India to Ethiopia, one hundred twenty-seven provinces
the army of Persia and Media, the nobles and princes of the provinces

stages.text: the provinces: a vast realm of 127 provinces spanning from India to Ethiopia; wide river plains, dry steppe and desert, date palms and tamarisk along irrigation canals, walled cities of sun-dried brick and stone with gates, royal roads with milestones, Persian palaces with columned halls, and village settlements of mudbrick houses.

fields.primarySubject: Mordecai, standing and holding an open scroll of the decree
fields.action: Mordecai unrolls the decree while Esther sits beside him, both attentive to the written words.
fields.setting: A palace court in Susa with stone columns, a plastered wall and a city gate visible beyond, under clear spring sky.
fields.secondaryElements: Esther seated on a low stool in royal blue robes; a scribe's writing case and reed pens on a stone bench; clay lamps unlit beside the wall.
fields.mood: Solemn and resolute, with quiet hope as the people's days are being fixed.
fields.timeOfDay: Midday warm golden sunlight with gentle shadows.
fields.composition: Medium shot from a low side angle, Mordecai on the left holding the scroll, Esther seated on the right, the gate in the background.

look.place: Royal Persian city of Susa and the provinces of the empire; palace courts, city gates, and Jewish village settlements
look.timeOfDay: Daytime, with a festive evening gathering implied; the section moves from solemn fasting to celebration
look.weather: Clear, warm spring sky with soft breezes
look.light: Warm golden sunlight with gentle shadows, transitioning to lamplit warmth in evening
look.clothing: Period tunics, cloaks and court robes in earth tones and royal blue; simple mourning sackcloth and ashes give way to festive garments

canon.name: Solomon
canon.note: Son of David and Bathsheba, king of Israel who builds the temple; the same individual across all divisions. Distinguish from the Shulammite's shepherd beloved, who is not Solomon.

stages.label: Solomon, king of Israel

quotes.quote: had Solomon ride on King David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon.
sat down on his throne and caused a throne to be set for the king’s mother

stages.text: Solomon: man in his twenties to forties, lean and upright with a composed, dignified bearing; warm olive-brown skin; dark curly hair and a short, neatly trimmed beard; calm, thoughtful face with a broad brow. Signature outfit: a long deep-blue royal court robe with gold-thread borders over a white linen tunic, and a gold circlet on his head. Signature prop: a plain rod of royal authority carried alone.

canon.name: Huram
canon.note: King of Tyre who sends cedar, craftsmen and supplies to Solomon; not the same as the craftsman Huram-abi.

stages.label: Huram, king of Tyre

quotes.quote: Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre
Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing

stages.text: Huram: man in middle years, around fifty; sturdy build; olive-brown skin; dark hair and short trimmed beard with some grey at the temples; dignified, weathered face with deep-set eyes and a straight nose. Signature outfit: a long purple-dyed court robe edged with woven gold thread over a white linen tunic. Signature prop: a plain cedar-wood staff of office.

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
canon.name: Jerusalem
canon.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

fields.primarySubject: Solomon, standing at the threshold of the house he built, in royal robes with a bearing of solemn resolve.
fields.action: Solomon turns to face Pharaoh’s daughter, who has just been brought up from David’s city, and gestures toward the house he built for her.
fields.setting: A stone-walled palace house on the rise of Jerusalem, with the city’s walls and rooftops visible below in the late light.
fields.secondaryElements: Pharaoh’s daughter in a fine Egyptian-styled linen gown and jewelry, attended by a few household servants; the path climbing up from David’s city behind them, dust still on the stones.
fields.mood: Solemn, dignified and reflective, with an undercurrent of weighty decision.
fields.timeOfDay: Late afternoon, warm low sunlight across the stone and the city.
fields.composition: Medium-wide shot from slightly below the threshold, Solomon in the left foreground and the woman and servants on the right, with the city of Jerusalem receding behind them.

look.place: Jerusalem: palace precincts and the Temple Mount with stone walls, cedar beams, and city gates
look.timeOfDay: Midday, bright and clear
look.weather: Dry, clear sky with light haze
look.light: Strong warm sunlight, long soft shadows on limestone
look.clothing: Tunics, cloaks and court robes of linen and wool; Huram in merchant dress with seafaring wraps

aliases: my child's father in the faith
the aged prisoner of Christ Jesus
canon.name: Paul the apostle
canon.note: The apostle Paul, author and speaker of all thirteen letters; the same individual across Romans, Corinthians, Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians, Thessalonians, Timothy, Titus and Philemon, identified by his apostolic authorship and first-person voice.

stages.label: Paul the apostle

quotes.quote: being such a one as Paul, the aged, but also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains.
I, Paul, write this with my own hand

stages.text: Paul the apostle: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifties to sixties, wiry and weathered from travel and imprisonment; Jewish Mediterranean features, olive-brown skin, short greying-dark beard and close-cropped hair receding at the temples; lined brow, steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark-blue cloak. Signature prop: a rolled parchment scroll and a reed pen case at the belt.

canon.name: The Corinthian believers
canon.note: The quarrelling assembly at Corinth addressed by Paul in 1 Corinthians; addressees rather than a stage group.

stages.label: The Corinthian believers

quotes.quote: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
For it has been reported to me concerning you, my brothers, by those who are from Chloe’s household, that there are contentions among you.
For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers.

stages.text: The Corinthian believers: a typical member is an adult of thirty to fifty years, of mixed Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean stock, with olive or light brown skin weathered by sea air and street life. Hair is dark or brown, worn short or tied back, with a clean-shaven or short-bearded face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre with a dark brown woollen cloak. Carries no props alone.

canon.name: Corinth
canon.note: The Greek city of Corinth, the setting of Paul's eighteen-month ministry in Acts, the church addressed in 1 and 2 Corinthians, and the place mentioned in Romans and 2 Timothy; all entries refer to the same city.

stages.label: Corinth

quotes.quote: After these things Paul departed from Athens and came to Corinth.

stages.text: Corinth: a Greek and Roman port city on a broad isthmus between two seas, with a steep citadel rising behind it. Limestone and brick houses and shops line straight streets; a stone forum with colonnaded porticoes, temples and a theatre stand at its centre. Olive groves, vines and pine trees cover the slopes beyond the walls.

fields.primarySubject: Paul the apostle standing and speaking with an open hand raised toward the gathered Corinthian believers.
fields.action: Paul addresses the believers, questioning how some among them deny the resurrection of the dead.
fields.setting: The stone agora of Corinth, with a colonnaded street and marketplace stalls behind the gathering.
fields.secondaryElements: Corinthian believers, Jewish and Gentile, listen in a close group with a few looking troubled; townspeople and merchants pass along the colonnade in the background.
fields.mood: Earnest, reverent and searching, with a tension of doubt and hope.
fields.timeOfDay: Late morning, bright warm sunlight from the south with soft shadows under the colonnades.
fields.composition: Medium shot from slightly below eye level, Paul on one side of the frame with the believers arranged in a loose arc facing him, colonnade receding behind.

look.place: Corinth, a Roman colonial city with a stone agora, colonnaded street and marketplace
look.timeOfDay: Daytime, late morning into early afternoon
look.weather: Clear, dry Mediterranean sky with a few scattered clouds
look.light: Bright warm sunlight from the south, soft shadows under colonnades
look.clothing: Tunics and cloaks of Jewish and Gentile townspeople; Roman civic dress in the city

canon.name: Moses
canon.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
canon.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
canon.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

aliases: Pharaoh (king of Egypt who did not know Joseph)
canon.name: Pharaoh of the Exodus (oppressor of Israel)
canon.note: The unnamed king of Egypt in Exodus who enslaves Israel, hardens his heart against Moses and suffers the plagues; the same king recalled in Deuteronomy and cited in Romans 9:17 as the one raised up to show God's power.

stages.label: Pharaoh of the Exodus

quotes.quote: The king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said to them
Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to them

stages.text: Pharaoh of the Exodus: man in his fifties, tall and broad-shouldered, dark brown skin; close-cropped hair under a blue-and-gold nemes headcloth, and a short trimmed false beard of the royal style; calm, hard features with heavy-lidded eyes and a firm mouth. Signature outfit: white linen kilt with a pleated gold-edged apron, broad gold collar, and red-and-gold royal sash. Signature props: gold crook and flail of royal office, carried alone.

canon.name: the Egyptians
canon.note: The Egyptian people, officers and magicians in Exodus who oppress Israel and suffer the plagues; distinguished from the Egyptian magicians of Genesis and from the Chaldeans of Babylon.

stages.label: the Egyptians

quotes.quote: The Egyptians ruthlessly made the children of Israel serve,
They also, the magicians of Egypt, did the same thing with their enchantments.

stages.text: the Egyptians: adults of middle age, broad-shouldered and strong from labour and rank, with warm brown skin and close-cropped black hair, clean-shaven men with short wigs or bare heads, dignified and grave of face. Signature outfit: a pleated white linen kilt or wrap-tunic with a linen cloak in ochre and blue. Signature props: none carried alone; officers may bear a staff of office.

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
canon.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
canon.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

canon.name: Red Sea
canon.note: The sea in Exodus that parts for Israel and closes over Pharaoh's army; distinct from the other seas by its setting in the exodus narrative.

stages.label: Red Sea

quotes.quote: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Yahweh caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night
the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
You shall encamp opposite it by the sea.

stages.text: Red Sea: a wide, deep arm of open water between desert shores, its surface dark blue-green under wind. Sand dunes and low reddish cliffs line the coast; scattered tamarisk and palms grow at the water's edge. Bare rock outcrops and shallow wadis run down to the shore, and a distant fortified town sits on the northern ridge.

canon.name: The wilderness (Exodus route)
canon.note: The desert stretches Israel travels from Egypt through Shur, Sin and Marah, with manna, quail and water miracles; the same wilderness as the Psalms and Amos references.

stages.label: The wilderness (Exodus route)

quotes.quote: they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.
on the surface of the wilderness was a small round thing, small as the frost on the ground.
in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.

stages.text: The wilderness: a vast arid tableland of pale sand, gravel plains and dark rock outcrops rising to bare mountains, scattered with thorn scrub and sparse grasses in the wadis. Tents and camp-circles mark the encampments; a distant mountain, Sinai, rises above the plain. Dry riverbeds, stone wells and rock fissures suggest hidden water.

fields.primarySubject: Pharaoh standing in the court, one hand raised toward his chest, face turned toward his servants
fields.action: Pharaoh and his servants shift their weight and turn toward each other in sudden doubt, the king's gaze fixed on the courtiers
fields.setting: An Egyptian royal court of painted stone and linen hangings, with a wide doorway opening onto the sunlit desert beyond
fields.secondaryElements: Several Egyptian servants and officials in linen kilts and collars gathered close, some with hands lifted; a bronze-fitted chariot waits at the doorway edge
fields.mood: Sudden unease and reckoning, heavy with grief and regret, restrained and solemn
fields.timeOfDay: Bright late-morning desert light falling through the doorway across the stone floor
fields.composition: Medium shot from the side of the court; Pharaoh centred at left, servants grouped toward the right, the open doorway framing the distant desert

look.place: Shore of a wide sea at the edge of a desert wilderness; sand, rock ledges and scattered tents of the Israelite camp, with dark Egyptian chariots approaching across a dry plain behind.
look.timeOfDay: Late evening turning to pre-dawn across the section, with the pursuit lit by the coming dawn.
look.weather: Still, heavy air after a dry day; low clouds gathering and a faint wind rising off the water.
look.light: Fading dusk warmth shifting to cool grey pre-dawn; a dense veiled cloud glowing with a brilliant white-gold light and a fire-like glow at its heart, as the permitted radiance of God's presence.
look.clothing: Israelite people in woven tunics and cloaks; Egyptian soldiers in linen and leather armour; chariot horses with bridles and trappings.

previous.text: As soon as he had finished speaking, behold, the king’s sons came, and lifted up their voices and wept. The king also and all his servants wept bitterly.

canon.name: Absalom
canon.note: Son of David who revolts and is killed by Joab.

stages.label: Absalom, son of David

quotes.quote: From the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no defect in him.
Absalom prepared a chariot and horses for himself, and fifty men to run before him.
Absalom was riding on his mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak

stages.text: Absalom: a young man of about twenty, lean and upright, with an unblemished, strikingly handsome face; olive-brown skin; thick dark hair worn long to the shoulders; a short, full beard trimmed close; dark, clear eyes. Signature outfit: a fine undyed linen tunic with a deep blue court cloak edged in gold thread. Signature prop: a mule, which he rides, and nothing else he carries alone.

aliases: the anointed of the God of Jacob
canon.name: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)
canon.note: The single David of the Hebrew books and the New Testament references: son of Jesse, shepherd, harpist, anointed king, father of Solomon; all entries describe this one king and the hint's second David is not needed.

stages.label: David as king

quotes.quote: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

stages.text: David: a man of about thirty to fifty, athletic and broad-shouldered, of medium height; ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes, short dark beard trimmed close; dark hair cut to the shoulder. Signature outfit: a long blue royal robe with a sash of crimson and gold, over an undertunic of white linen. Carries a bronze-bossed sword in a leather scabbard and a harp.

stages.label: David as youth

quotes.quote: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”

stages.text: David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.

stages.label: David as elder

quotes.quote: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.

stages.text: David: an old man of about seventy, lean and bent with age, his frame still dignified; ruddy complexion faded to a weathered warmth, dark eyes deep-set and gentle, white hair and a white beard cut short. Signature outfit: a plain long wool robe of undyed cream with a dark blue cloak over the shoulders for warmth. Carries a staff of almond wood.

canon.name: Jonadab son of Shimeah
canon.note: David's nephew, son of Shimeah and Amnon's friend in 2 Samuel who devises the plot against Tamar; distinct from Jonadab son of Rechab.

stages.label: Jonadab son of Shimeah

quotes.quote: Jonadab was a very subtle man.

stages.text: Jonadab son of Shimeah: a man in his late twenties to thirties; lean, medium build; olive skin; short dark beard trimmed close; narrow, watchful face with a thoughtful brow. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of dark blue-grey wool beneath a court robe of deep ochre, with a plain linen headcloth. He carries no props.

canon.name: David's royal palace in Jerusalem
canon.note: The king's house in Jerusalem where David's scenes unfold (Bathsheba, Uriah, Nathan, Amnon and Tamar); distinguish from the other royal houses by its Davidic setting.

stages.label: David's royal palace in Jerusalem

quotes.quote: went up to the room over the gate and wept

stages.text: David's royal palace in Jerusalem: a substantial citadel of dressed ashlar stone and cedar-beamed timber, set on the ridge of the City of David above the Kidron valley. Flat-roofed stone halls rise in terraces, with a gate tower of heavy masonry whose upper chamber, the room over the gate, has latticed windows. Olive trees and terraced vineyards grow on the slopes below; cypress and terebinth stand near the walls.

fields.primarySubject: David, king of Israel, seated and grieving alone.
fields.action: He sits motionless, head bowed and hands clasped, in mourning, with no one else in the courtyard reacting at this instant.
fields.setting: The royal palace courtyard in Jerusalem, stone paving and garden greenery under a dry, clear sky.
fields.secondaryElements: Sackcloth mourning garments on David; dust hanging in the warm light; the empty courtyard around him.
fields.mood: Quiet, heavy grief held with dignity.
fields.timeOfDay: Day, warm golden sunlight in the palace.
fields.composition: Medium-wide view from the courtyard edge, David placed off-center in the foreground, the palace architecture rising behind him.

look.place: Royal palace courtyard and gardens in Jerusalem, later a road and hill country toward Geshur
look.timeOfDay: Day, with a change from daylight in the palace to dusk on the journey
look.weather: Dry, clear sky with dust in the air
look.light: Warm golden sunlight shifting to soft evening amber
look.clothing: Tunics and cloaks of undyed wool, travel cloaks for flight, mourning garments of sackcloth

moment.text: So the priests and the Levites, with some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants, lived in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.

previous.text: They gave according to their ability into the treasury of the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priests’ garments.

canon.name: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel
canon.note: Governor of Judah who leads the return from exile and the temple rebuilding; the single individual across Ezra, Nehemiah, Haggai and Zechariah, distinguished from the high priest Joshua.

stages.label: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel

quotes.quote: I will take you, Zerubbabel my servant, the son of Shealtiel
to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah
will make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you

stages.text: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and steady in bearing; olive skin weathered by travel; dark hair and a short, neatly kept beard with some early grey; a grave, resolute face with deep-set dark eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo wool cloak fastened at the shoulder, with a governor's embroidered band of red and gold at the hem. Carries alone a bronze signet ring on his right hand.

canon.name: Jeshua son of Jozadak (high priest, builder of the altar)
canon.note: High priest son of Jozadak who builds the altar with Zerubbabel in Ezra; the same high priest appears in Nehemiah's genealogies, distinct from Levite Jeshuas.

stages.label: Jeshua son of Jozadak, high priest

canon.note: The city and empire of exile and captivity across the prophets, histories and psalms, also called Babylonia, Shinar and the land of the Chaldeans; the same place in every division.

stages.label: Babylon

fields.mood: Quiet resettlement, a fragile sense of belonging after exile.

canon.note: Exiled priest and prophet at the river Chebar.

stages.text: Ezekiel son of Buzi: a man of about thirty, lean and steady, with dark hair and a short trimmed beard, bronze-brown skin from desert sun, and a calm, watchful face. canon.name: Man clothed in linen
canon.note: Heavenly figure who marks the faithful with a mark, scatters coals over the city, and measures the new temple with a reed; treated as one guide throughout Ezekiel.

stages.label: Man clothed in linen

quotes.quote: the man clothed in linen, who had the writer’s inkhorn by his side
Take fire from between the whirling wheels, from between the cherubim

stages.text: Man clothed in linen: a figure of mature, steady presence, neither young nor old; lean and upright build; pale bronze skin with a faint radiance; close-cut dark hair and short beard; calm, grave features. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic and priestly linen sash, plain and unadorned. Carries a scribe's bronze inkhorn at his side and a measuring reed of cane in hand.

canon.name: Ezekiel's temple
canon.note: The Jerusalem temple of Ezekiel's visions of abominations and the measured new temple.

stages.label: Ezekiel's temple

quotes.quote: so that there was the face of a man toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other side.
There were made on them, on the doors of the nave, cherubim and palm trees, like those made on the walls.
He measured the court, one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide, square. The altar was before the house.

stages.text: Ezekiel's temple: a walled sanctuary on the mountain of Jerusalem, built of pale dressed limestone with cedar panelling, its inner court paved and square, its nave carved with cherubim and palm trees between which a face of a man and a face of a young lion alternate. Gates of the outer court face east, north and south; side chambers rise in three stories. Olive and cedar trees line the courts; a river flows from beneath the threshold.

fields.secondaryElements: Measuring cord and reed in the man's hands; dust haze over the ground; no veiled cloud or radiance in the scene.
fields.mood: Quiet, attentive and orderly, with a sense of careful measurement.
fields.timeOfDay: Early morning, low even light falling across the stone.
fields.composition: Medium shot from the court looking toward the south gate; the gatepost and linen figure in the foreground, Ezekiel at the side, the arch and plateau behind.

canon.name: Moses
canon.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

canon.name: Aaron, brother of Moses
canon.note: Moses' older brother and first high priest, in Exodus and in Numbers (census, offerings, death on Mount Hor); the same man across both divisions.

stages.label: Aaron, the first high priest

quotes.quote: Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses.
Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, they made finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron
Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

stages.text: Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.

canon.name: The Levites
canon.note: The tribe of Levi serving in the tabernacle and carrying its furnishings in Numbers.

stages.label: The Levites

quotes.quote: The Levites purified themselves from sin, and they washed their clothes
from twenty-five years old and upward they shall go in to wait on the service

stages.text: The Levites: men from twenty-five years old upward, of mature working age; sturdy, unhurried build from carrying the tabernacle frames and furnishings; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard; calm, dignified features. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a cloak of undyed wool, washed clean; a wooden carrying pole across the shoulders.

aliases: the mountain that might be touched
canon.name: Horeb/Mount Sinai
canon.note: The single mountain of God where the law and covenant are given; all listed entries (Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Malachi, Hebrews) refer to the same mountain under the names Horeb, Sinai, God's mountain, referenced across divisions.

stages.label: Horeb/Mount Sinai

quotes.quote: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire
You shall set bounds to the people all around
the cloud covered it six days
The mountain burned with fire to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

stages.text: Horeb/Mount Sinai: a single steep granite mountain rising from a stark desert wilderness of rock and sand; its lower slopes are broken boulders and gravel, its upper peak sharp and dark, with a cloud-wrapped summit. The base is marked by a rocky plain where the people camp, bounded by stones. No vegetation beyond scattered desert shrub; the mountain has no buildings.

canon.name: the tabernacle (portable sanctuary)
canon.note: The one portable sanctuary of the wilderness, described in Exodus 25-40 and referred to as the Tent of Meeting in Leviticus and Numbers; all three entries are the same place.

stages.label: The tabernacle (portable sanctuary)

quotes.quote: made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet. They made them with cherubim
He made curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle.
He made the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side southward.
the sockets around the court, the sockets of the gate of the court, all the pins of the tabernacle

stages.text: The tabernacle: a portable sanctuary of a rectangular tent of fine twined linen curtains in blue, purple and scarlet woven with cherubim, over a covering of goats' hair and rams' skins, stretched over upright acacia boards overlaid with gold, set in silver sockets and held by gold-covered bars, enclosed by a court of white linen hangings on bronze pillars.

fields.primarySubject: Moses and Aaron standing side by side at the eastern entrance, Moses holding a tally cord while Aaron records the count on a tablet.

fields.mood: Solemn, orderly and dignified, with quiet attentiveness among the families.
fields.timeOfDay: Clear late morning light falling across the sanctuary and the gathered ranks.
fields.composition: Wide frontal view; the tabernacle entrance centred behind Moses and Aaron, with the Levite ranks receding in rows toward the viewer's left.

canon.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord
canon.note: The one Jesus: the teacher from Nazareth of the Gospels and Acts, and the risen, exalted Christ and Lord of the epistles and Revelation; the same individual across all divisions, with death, resurrection and changed portrayal not creating new individuals.

stages.label: Adult Jesus

quotes.quote: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

stages.text: Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

stages.label: Infant Jesus

quotes.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

canon.name: the Pharisees
canon.note: The Pharisees as a religious party opposing Jesus over Sabbath, purity, tradition and table fellowship; all four Gospel entries describe this same party, so they form one cluster.

stages.label: the Pharisees

quotes.quote: The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat.
like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful

stages.text: The Pharisees: a typical member of the party is a man of middle age to elderly, with a lean, serious build; olive skin weathered by travel; a close-cut or short-bearded face with a grave, watchful expression; hair kept neatly under a head covering. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a dark blue-violet cloak and tassel fringes at the corners. Signature prop: a small phylactery box on the forehead and forearm, and a scroll of the law.

canon.name: Galilee
canon.note: The northern region of Galilee where Jesus preaches, teaches and heals; both Matthew and Luke describe the same region, so these entries are one place.

stages.label: Galilee

stages.text: Galilee: Northern hill country falling to a freshwater lake, the sea of Galilee, its shore lined with fishing boats and nets drying on stone. Low limestone villages of flat-roofed houses, a white stone synagogue with a shallow portico, terraced olive groves, fig trees and scrubland. Roman roads and a distant Gentile town on the slopes.

canon.name: The righteous (Psalms)
canon.note: The collective of the godly and humble who trust Yahweh and suffer oppression across the Psalms; distinct from the remnant of Judah, which is a specific Judahite community addressed by Zephaniah.

stages.label: The righteous (Psalms)

quotes.quote: My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.
For the needy shall not always be forgotten, nor the hope of the poor perish forever.
He raises up the poor out of the dust, and lifts up the needy from the ash heap,

stages.text: The righteous: adults of mixed age, mostly middle-aged, lean and sturdy from farm and road labour; olive to brown skin; dark hair kept short or tied back, men with trimmed beards; plain, careworn faces, dignified and steady. Signature outfit: undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre and earth tones with a plain brown woollen cloak. Signature prop: a simple staff or walking stick.

canon.name: The wilderness (Exodus route)
canon.note: The desert stretches Israel travels from Egypt through Shur, Sin and Marah, with manna, quail and water miracles; the same wilderness as the Psalms and Amos references.

stages.label: The wilderness (Exodus route)

quotes.quote: they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.
on the surface of the wilderness was a small round thing, small as the frost on the ground.
in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.

stages.text: The wilderness: a vast arid tableland of pale sand, gravel plains and dark rock outcrops rising to bare mountains, scattered with thorn scrub and sparse grasses in the wadis. Tents and camp-circles mark the encampments; a distant mountain, Sinai, rises above the plain. Dry riverbeds, stone wells and rock fissures suggest hidden water.

fields.primarySubject: Radiance of great light and cloud, representing the sovereign God, with no human face or body.
fields.action: The light rises and spreads in majesty over the earth, a silent proclamation of kingship above all gods.
fields.setting: A vast open sky over a broad landscape of hills and distant mountains, lit from above.
fields.secondaryElements: Rolling clouds catching golden light; distant mountain peaks below in the glow; no figures present.
fields.mood: Reverent, awe-filled, steady and majestic.
fields.timeOfDay: Early morning light breaking across the sky.
fields.composition: Wide, low-angle view looking up toward the radiant sky, with the mountains and horizon anchoring the lower part of the frame.

canon.name: Noah
canon.note: The righteous patriarch of Genesis who builds the ark, survives the flood, and has sons Shem, Ham and Japheth; the same Noah is alluded to in Matthew, Hebrews, 1 Peter and 2 Peter as a historical example, so all Noah entries form one cluster.

stages.label: Noah

quotes.quote: Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time. Noah walked with God.
Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters came on the earth.

stages.text: Noah: man of about six hundred years, weathered and sturdy from a lifetime of farming and shipbuilding; broad-shouldered, lean, with deep lines at the eyes and brow; skin sun-browned; long grey hair and a full grey beard, kept untrimmed; calm, steady, dignified face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic in earth brown under a rough wool wrap in ochre, with leather sandals. Carries a carpenter's adze or a simple wooden staff, nothing else.

canon.name: Noah's ark
canon.note: The gopher-wood vessel built at God's command to carry Noah's family and the animals through the flood; not a ship at sea in the Jonah or Acts sense.

stages.label: The ark

quotes.quote: Make a ship of gopher wood. You shall make rooms in the ship
The length of the ship shall be three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
You shall make a roof in the ship, and you shall finish it to a cubit upward. You shall set the door of the ship in its side.
You shall make it with lower, second, and third levels.

stages.text: Noah's ark: a vast wooden vessel of gopher wood, roughly three hundred cubits long, fifty wide and thirty high, built in three levels with a roof finished a cubit upward. Its planks are sealed inside and out with dark pitch. A single door is set in its side. Its timbers are weathered grey-brown where the flood water has washed over them.

fields.primarySubject: Noah's ark, a large wooden vessel floating on the open floodwaters.
fields.action: The ark rides buoyantly on the surface of the rising waters, its hull lifted clear of the land.
fields.setting: A wide expanse of brown floodwater stretching to the horizon, with the tops of distant hills barely visible through the rising flood.
fields.secondaryElements: Dark grey clouds hang low over the water; a faint drift of debris floats near the hull. No human figures are shown on the deck at this instant.
fields.mood: Solemn, awe-filled and quietly sorrowful, with a sense of vast loss held in stillness.
fields.timeOfDay: Overcast daylight with diffused grey light across the water.
fields.composition: Wide view from a low angle across the water, the ark placed centrally on the surface with the horizon and clouds filling the frame above.
